I would like to sincerely apologize for my previous comment, where I referred to your question as “stupid.” That was thoughtless and disrespectful, and I deeply regret it. Your question was valid, and I understand that as someone who is still learning, seeking help is an important part of the process.

At the same time, I believe that as a newcomer, it’s important to try solving problems on our own to the best of our ability before seeking help, especially for questions that are unrelated to the core function of the project. This helps reduce unnecessary distractions and ensures that we can focus on improving and maintaining the project. I also realize that open-source contributors give their time and effort to help others, and we should respect their energy by asking relevant and thoughtful questions.

Thank you for your understanding, and I will approach such situations with more consideration in the future.

title: Minimum and recommended configuration
body: I would like to ask what are the minimum and recommended configurations for a computer and what are the GPU requirements?
author: TAMTAM0122

comments.body:
It depends on whether you're using LLMs via API calls or serving them locally.

# LLM Recommendations:

For the language model that is critical to completion, use models with 70B or more parameters, such as Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. 

For the vision model that primarily involves image captioning, models with 7B or more parameters like Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct are suitable.

# System Requirements:
The system has been tested on Linux, with at least 8GB RAM. You'll need LibreOffice and other specified dependencies installed.
# GPU Requirements(using LLMs via API calls):
A graphics card with 8GB VRAM or more is sufficient to handle both embedding models and PDF parsing models for markers.

# GPU Requirements(using LLMs via self-hosting):
A GPU cluster with at least 80GB VRAM is sufficient to serve quantized models with 77B+ parameters.
Does it support CPU operation?

> Does it support CPU operation?

I believe it's ok, just change cuda symbols in backend.py, but it will cost a lot more times I guess

I am just simply using a modification of backend.py, to run it locally with gpt-4o. Which function should I debug for this issue?

Great work, btw.
author: mjshz

comments.body:
The incorporation of images is automatically determined by LLMs, so we currently do not have a way to insert specific images manually. 

However, you might try refining the role definition of the planner to influence the output.

Lastly, thank you for your kind words! 
Feel free to reach out if you have any further questions.
😀
